title: Hexapod · Development roadmap
mission: Hexapod MKII: from walking to autonomous surveying
description: Build a hexapod that surveys an area drawn on a map and returns a 3D map of the ground. It can stop to take measurements and process the finished map afterward.

nodes.title: Draw the survey area
nodes.label: Interface to build
nodes.meaning: The operator draws the boundary on a map. The boundary and robot position use coordinates relative to the same test site.
nodes.input: A map and the operator’s boundary

nodes.title: Plan the survey route
nodes.label: Planner to build
nodes.meaning: Choose a route and measurement stops that cover the requested area. The first course is level, hard and clear of obstacles.
nodes.input: Survey boundary, ground map and robot position

nodes.title: Set speed and direction
nodes.label: Command types and follower example
nodes.meaning: You can pass forward speed, sideways speed and yaw rate through shared command types and the waypoint follower example. Route planning and qualified runtime integration remain pending.
nodes.output: Forward speed, sideways speed, turning rate and stop

nodes.title: Control the gait
nodes.label: PPO videos recorded; gait still unqualified
nodes.meaning: Researchers replayed an optimized forward trajectory that passes its native screen. The tested PPO policies fail walking acceptance. The current kernel supports stock PPO; the paper motion-prior method remains to be implemented.
nodes.input: Requested motion, joint positions and body motion

nodes.title: Measure the surroundings
nodes.label: M1: test scope agreed
nodes.meaning: The first test uses a simulated Mid-360 laser scanner. Save a scan of a known floor and wall, then reload it and check the measured geometry. The physical sensor is not mounted.
nodes.input: Simulated laser distances and sensor position
nodes.output: Recorded 3D points and flags identifying valid measurements

nodes.title: Track robot position
nodes.label: Estimator to build
nodes.meaning: Combine sensor and movement measurements to track the robot’s position and orientation within the test site.
nodes.input: Laser scans, motion measurements and sensor calibration
nodes.output: Estimated position, orientation, speed and error

nodes.title: Map the nearby ground
nodes.label: Historical synthetic-data prototype
nodes.meaning: Researchers tested synthetic ground-height observations in the archived prototype. Current map assembly and localization remain pending. Mapping issue #19 uses simulator-provided poses for its first combined map.
nodes.input: Scans aligned using the estimated sensor position
nodes.output: Nearby ground heights and measurement uncertainty

nodes.title: Drive the joints
nodes.label: Simulation model prepared
nodes.meaning: Apply limits to joint movement and motor torque before sending targets to the motors. Check the simulated response against measurements from the planned leg test stand.
nodes.output: Motor commands and measured joint movement

nodes.title: Train in simulation
nodes.label: Stock PPO kernel; paper implementation pending
nodes.meaning: Researchers completed one- and 128-robot standing admission and PPO runs on frozen source packs. Use locomotion/ for current code and TRAINING for the reproduction order. A new source allocation needs matching native admission.
nodes.input: Robot model, physics settings and training task

nodes.title: Test movement and stops
nodes.label: Policy tests recorded; walking still unqualified
nodes.meaning: Researchers evaluated the paired PPO arms at updates 0, 300, 600 and 1200. Both fail the scheduled forward tests and final quiet-stop diagnostics. The kernel provides 13 diagnostic probes and 96 Stage 2 cases, with contact-force and motor-torque recording. Full qualification and human gait acceptance remain pending.
nodes.input: A saved controller and fixed test cases
nodes.output: Measurements and a pass or fail result

nodes.title: Test a physical leg
nodes.label: Test stand planned
nodes.meaning: Measure force and joint position on a single-leg test stand. Compare those measurements with the same setup in simulation before testing a complete robot.
nodes.input: Leg test stand, force sensor and joint encoder
nodes.output: Measured differences between the physical leg and simulation

nodes.title: Produce the survey map
nodes.label: Final goal
nodes.meaning: Follow the survey route, stop at measurement locations and hold the sensor platform steady. Combine the measurements into a 3D terrain map after the run.
nodes.input: Survey route, robot position and recorded scans
nodes.output: A 3D terrain map covering the requested area

milestones.description: Qualify signed translation, turns, transitions and quiet stops on the approved model. Historical standing admissions apply to their frozen sources; obtain matching admission for a new allocation.

milestones.title: Survey a drawn area
milestones.description: Follow a route through the requested area, stop with a steady sensor platform to scan, and deliver a 3D terrain map. Start on a level, hard surface with no obstacles.

milestones.question: Assign owners and reviewers for #19 mapping and #20 survey rehearsal. Preserve the M1 fixture; define combined-map error and mission-rehearsal limits before their tests.

definition.title: Save and reload one simulated laser scan
definition.summary: Use a stationary Mid-360 laser scanner in simulation to measure a known floor and wall. Save the 3D points, reload them in a separate check, and compare them with the scene. This task can start before walking works.
criteria: Reload the points, validity flags and sensor position and orientation without changing their values.
With noise disabled, every expected floor or wall hit must be within 1 mm of its expected position.
With the existing sensor noise enabled, at least 95% of expected hits must be within 7 cm. Missing hits count as failures; report false hits separately.
definition.fixture: Sensor height: 0.25 m. Wall: 0.80 m wide × 0.08 m thick × 0.50 m high, centred 1 m in front of the sensor. Use 20,000 rays per scan. Fixed random seeds: 360 for the scan pattern and 20260824 for sensor noise and timing.

milestones.card_text: Pending canonical qualification; M1 scope retained.

papers.title: Learning Natural and Robust Hexapod Locomotion over Complex Terrains via Motion Priors based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.role: Target simulation method: PPO with a motion prior and asymmetric training. Implementation follows the proposed TRAINING sequence.

glossary.meaning: A trained model that selects joint targets from the requested movement and the robot’s measured state.
One adjustment to the controller based on its simulated experience. Update count alone does not measure walking quality.
A collection of 3D points measured by a laser scanner.
Positions measured relative to a reference at the test site, rather than latitude and longitude.
The measurements and limits a test must satisfy before its result is accepted.
The laser scanner selected for the first mapping test. M1 uses its simulation model.

progress.summary: Researchers passed the optimized forward-trajectory screen, but the tested PPO policies fail walking acceptance. The paired initialization test found no benefit in its one seed. The consolidated kernel supports the proposed simulation-reproduction order in TRAINING; paper-method implementation and fresh-source native admission remain pending.
progress.definition_policy: Use issue #18 for walking, #19 for simulated mapping and #20 for mission rehearsal. Preserve the approved model and numerical gates. Record contact force and motor torque in native evaluations; these loads add no acceptance limits. Follow TRAINING for the proposed reproduction order.

facts.title: Exact one- and 128-robot standing admission adopted
facts.backend: Lead-reviewed simulation standing admission002 · confirmed mass-corrected model · full independent raw audit
facts.text: The lead adopted one002 and all 128 rescored batch128 replicas with matching model/controller/layout identity and contact checks. Raw captures remain on Spark with hash-bound metadata. This standing admission covers its frozen source; the consolidated source requires fresh admission before training.

facts.title: Improved optimized reference passes the forward screen
facts.backend: One admitted Isaac Sim replica; 1000 controls and 8000 recorded physics steps; no PPO
facts.text: The optimizer adds root-speed tracking and a target-curvature term. Native planar tracking error falls from 0.033271 to 0.003029 m/s against the unchanged 0.025 m/s limit. The robot moves 0.974348 m forward in 20 seconds. The audit verifies 36 transferred files, reproduces servo targets and reclassifies 130821 contact patches. Native motor, joint and contact checks pass. This one-command result does not qualify turning, stopping or Stage 2.

facts.title: The saved PPO policy fails forward, quiet and stop probes
facts.backend: One admitted Isaac Sim replica; final checkpoint1200; 3050 controls and 24400 physics samples
facts.text: The audit reproduces the original verdicts and reclassifies 530534 contact patches. CPU inference from the saved weights matches recorded actions within 0.00000144. Forward tracking error is 0.051091 m/s against the unchanged 0.025 m/s bound; mean forward speed is 0.000423 m/s. Quiet includes three native joint-speed violations and stopping includes one nonfoot contact sample. All cases retain complete videos and force summaries. Stage 2 remains incomplete.

facts.title: Example initialization produces no passing forward checkpoint
facts.backend: Native Isaac Sim; approved detailed model; one paired seed; equal PPO budgets; unchanged 0.040 rad per 20 ms limiter
facts.text: Each arm completed 1200 updates and 3686400 transitions. Both fail forward tests at updates 0, 300, 600 and 1200; the copied actor fails before PPO. Final mean speeds are 0.004811 m/s from scratch and 0.000961 m/s after initialization against 0.05 m/s. Planar errors are 0.051045 and 0.053322 m/s against the 0.025 m/s bound. Both fail motor-demand and quiet-stop checks. The benefit rule fails for this seed; other seeds and AMP remain untested.

facts.title: We record force and motor load for both final policies
facts.backend: 400 Hz native captures; 18-second forward window after two seconds of settling
facts.text: Mean vertical ground support is 73.246 N for scratch and 73.227 N for example initialization. Mean absolute applied motor torque is 0.488782 and 0.405900 N·m. Per-foot forces and per-joint requested and applied torque remain in the force summaries. These values describe failed, low-speed motions and do not establish efficiency at matched walking speed.

facts.title: Prescribed tripod controller passes CPU checks
facts.backend: CPU fixtures and approved-model kinematics; no native motion run
facts.text: The prescribed controller passes 17 CPU checks for phasing, contact transitions and stopping. The user deferred native runs after the GPU jobs stopped with preserved restart records. Native admission, terrain and Stage 2 remain incomplete.

facts.title: Tripod standing admission passes; motion tracking fails
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; approved 19-body robot; native 400 Hz capture
facts.text: One-robot and 32-robot standing admission pass with local raw recomputation. Fifteen motion attempts retain force, torque and video evidence. The first completed forward and turn screens fail tracking. Remaining timing choices and criteria 4–5/7 remain pending; Stage 2 and terrain stay incomplete.

facts.title: We measure incompatible tripod stance targets
facts.backend: Isaac Sim capture; controls 190–262; approved-model forward kinematics
facts.text: The measured cycle lasts 1.46 seconds with 0.26 seconds of touchdown waits. Two target stance-triangle edges vary by 27.9–28.6 mm per half-cycle. Median speed is 0.0081 m/s against a 0.05 m/s command. We retain the failed motion and inspect geometry mapping before further adaptations.

facts.title: We complete the declared tripod sweep with no passing motion
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; 24 native motion trials across recorded source corrections
facts.text: All four candidates fail the corrected larger-lift screens. The slower 0.12 rad choice has 0.03736 m/s forward tracking error and two native speed-bound violations. The slower 0.18 rad choice stops forward motion at control 615 with touchdown_timeout. Both fail both turns. We retain all 24 failed attempts and keep stops, clearance qualification and terrain pending.

facts.title: We derive tripod targets from the approved leg geometry
facts.backend: CPU kinematics and contact fixtures; native motion unqualified
facts.text: We declare two geometry candidates with uniform phase and pitch motion during support. The first 0.05 m/s trajectory reduces the maximum stance-edge range to 1.3 mm. Both candidates pass joint bounds and contact-transition fixtures. The 12/16 mm lift gates and native motion thresholds remain unchanged.

facts.title: We complete six geometry screens without a tracking pass
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; six 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Both geometry candidates pass native motor and contact checks but fail forward and yaw tracking. Mean forward speed reaches 0.0466 and 0.0513 m/s; tracking errors remain 0.0490 and 0.0535 m/s against 0.025. The recorded cycle has no touchdown wait and a 1.83 mm stance-edge range, but it retains surge and recoil. We retain thirty failed motion attempts.

facts.title: We declare a damping correction for joint tracking
facts.backend: CPU motor-law and contact-transition checks; native motion unqualified
facts.text: One candidate adds nominal joint-velocity feedforward through the existing motor-target input. Motor gains and limits remain unchanged. CPU replay adds at most 0.0332 rad and preserves the action envelope and 0.040 rad slew bound. Native qualification remains pending.

facts.title: We complete the damping screen without a tracking pass
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Native motor and contact checks pass. Mean forward speed reaches 0.04979 m/s, but tracking error remains 0.04852 m/s against 0.025. Left and right yaw errors remain 0.15315 and 0.15304 rad/s against 0.06. We retain 33 failed completed motion trials.

facts.title: We declare a phase clock and retain an interrupted native attempt
facts.backend: CPU path and target checks; partial Isaac Sim capture; native motion unqualified
facts.text: The declared clock retains the joint path and changes its timing, with unchanged motor limits and gates. CPU checks cover contact transitions, stops and both clearance modes. The launcher detected unrelated CUDA compute and removed its owned container. We retain 800 substeps from controls 0–99 with no final motion score; native launches await allocation coordination.

facts.title: We reduce tracking error with the phase clock
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Forward error falls to 0.03031 m/s and left/right yaw errors to 0.08860/0.08894 rad/s, above the unchanged 0.025 and 0.06 gates. Native motor and contact checks pass. The recorded forward cycle has 17% negative-speed controls, with support-joint errors above swing errors. We retain 36 failed completed trials and one interrupted attempt.

facts.title: We declare bounded joint feedback through motor targets
facts.backend: CPU encoder/contact replay and transition fixtures; native motion unqualified
facts.text: Two candidates add proportional joint-error feedback with gains 0.5 and 1.0. Each correction stays within 0.070 rad. Recorded-input replay preserves the joint/action envelope and 0.040 rad slew limit; it does not establish native stability. Actuator gains, torque-speed limits and acceptance gates remain unchanged.

facts.title: We retain three failed feedback screens
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Gain 0.5 produces forward error 0.03333 m/s and left/right yaw errors 0.08784/0.08813 rad/s. All three exceed tracking gates. The forward trial also has one speed violation and one nonfoot-contact substep during a 202 N rear-right toe impulse. We retain 39 failed completed trials and one interrupted attempt. Gain 1.0 remains unexecuted.

facts.title: We test lift timing within the target envelope
facts.backend: CPU replay of six recorded command/contact sequences and transition fixtures; native motion unqualified
facts.text: One revised candidate uses positive cos(phase)^1.5 swing lift with the same peak, period and hip sweep. Joint feedback stays off. We rejected cos(phase) before dispatch because it exceeded the target envelope at 0.10 m/s. The revised profile passes target checks through both clearance modes and stops; it supplies no native acceptance.

facts.title: We isolate joint motion in the failed lift screen
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Forward error is 0.02979 m/s and left/right yaw errors are 0.08488/0.08488 rad/s. All three exceed tracking gates; native motor and contact checks pass. Across 12 forward cycles, joint tracking contributes 0.0318–0.0334 m/s RMS to body speed and toe-marker motion contributes 0.0006–0.0020 m/s. We retain 42 failed completed trials and one interrupted attempt.

facts.title: We declare bounded velocity-error damping
facts.backend: CPU motor-law checks, recorded-input replay and stance approximation; native motion unqualified
facts.text: One candidate adds velocity-error feedback through motor targets with position feedback off. Each correction stays within 0.070 rad; joint/action bounds and the 0.040 rad slew limit remain active. A scalar stance approximation predicts weak body damping. Native screening must establish whether the added feedback reduces oscillation.

facts.title: We retain the sampled-feedback yaw failure
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: The forward trial meets the planar-error gate at 0.02195 m/s but fails yaw tracking at 0.11454 rad/s. Left/right yaw errors are 0.11713/0.11646 rad/s. All native motor/contact checks pass. The forward yaw spectrum peaks at 25 Hz. We retain 45 failed completed trials and one interrupted attempt.

facts.title: We filter velocity feedback at the control sample rate
facts.backend: CPU free-leg sampled model, transition checks and recorded-input replay; native motion unqualified
facts.text: The fixed-base free-leg linearization has spectral radius 1.524 with unfiltered gain-2 feedback and 0.854 with a 5 Hz filter. One candidate filters reference and measured joint velocity before the same bounded correction. CPU checks preserve target bounds; contact, saturation and native acceptance remain outside the linear model.

facts.title: We pass one forward screen and retain two turn failures
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Filtered velocity feedback passes the 0.05 m/s forward screen with planar error 0.02292 m/s and yaw error 0.01674 rad/s. Left/right yaw errors of 0.07747/0.07711 rad/s exceed 0.06. All native motor/contact checks pass. Across retained attempts, one completed screen passes, 47 fail and one attempt is interrupted. Stops, clearance and repeats remain pending.

facts.title: We combine bounded position and filtered velocity feedback
facts.backend: CPU sampled free-leg models and recorded-input replay; native qualification pending
facts.text: One declared candidate combines position gain 0.5 with velocity gain 2 and a 5 Hz filter. Its sampled-loop spectral radius stays below 0.802 across 2520 pose/leg models. The gain-1 combination fails the neutral-pose stability check and remains excluded. Six captured command replays preserve target and slew bounds. Native contact and saturation remain outside this linear analysis.

facts.title: We retain a forward pass and diagnose contact overlap
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Combined position and filtered velocity feedback passes forward motion at 0.02242 m/s planar error. Left/right yaw errors of 0.07587/0.07574 rad/s exceed 0.06. All native motor/contact checks pass. Across twelve left-turn cycles, yaw stops or reverses during six-foot contact. The accumulated record contains two passed screens, 49 failed completed trials and one interrupted attempt.

facts.title: We align yaw targets through support overlap
facts.backend: CPU phasing, command transitions and recorded-input replay; native qualification pending
facts.text: One declared candidate keeps horizontal yaw targets in support motion before phase 0.15 and after phase 0.80. Landed feet retain a pitch lift residual while the horizontal baseline continues. The full forward overlap probe exceeds target bounds and remains excluded; forward targets preserve the preceding candidate. Six recorded-input replays preserve emitted bounds, with target clipping during changed yaw traces.

facts.title: We pass forward and both turn screens
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; three 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Forward planar error is 0.02242 m/s. Left/right yaw errors are 0.03448/0.03478 rad/s against the unchanged 0.06 limit. All native motor/contact checks pass. A complete left-turn cycle retains yaw through six-foot contact after the declared overlap change. The accumulated record contains five passed screens, 49 failed completed trials and one interrupted attempt. Canonical 0.10 m/s motion, stops, raised clearance and independent repeats remain pending.

facts.title: We retain the canonical forward startup failure
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; incomplete canonical qualification; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: The canonical 0.10 m/s forward trial fails after 51 controls with support loss during startup. Left-front and right-rear feet lose support as the six planted feet move toward opposing stride endpoints. Requested torque peaks at 4.61 Nm; the motor retains its 1.6 Nm cap. Standing and the right-turn case pass. The owner stops the allocation during the next turn and retains its partial capture and exact cleanup.

facts.title: We build forward stride during tripod stepping
facts.backend: CPU startup, reset, command changes and recorded-input replay; native qualification pending
facts.text: The new candidate holds its standing reference during forward startup, then ramps stride over one gait cycle. It retains yaw startup and returns the yaw touchdown lift offset before the next half-cycle. The preceding controller and initial correction both exceed bounds in an early raised-touchdown fixture; the corrected candidate passes that fixture and 172 locomotion tests. The forward_high suite retains the canonical 0.10 m/s case and two independent resets.

facts.title: We correct the startup recording type
facts.backend: Isaac Sim recording failure; CPU serialization regression; native retry pending
facts.text: The first startup attempt stops after three controls because its new log field contains a NumPy boolean. It provides no walking result. The correction converts that field to a Python boolean and passes a regression test with a NumPy command. The retry retains the controller method, physics and acceptance limits.

facts.title: We pass startup and retain two forward tracking failures
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; two independent resets; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Both 0.10 m/s trials complete 1,000 controls without a controller fault. Mean speed is 0.09346 m/s; mean planar error is 0.05023 m/s against 0.025. Computed torque exceeds the unchanged demand-fraction bound. During one complete cycle, six-foot contact coincides with near-zero speed, followed by a surge after lift-off. Joint tracking contributes 0.04569 m/s RMS; toe-marker motion contributes 0.00324 m/s.

facts.title: We match forward support motion through ground overlap
facts.backend: CPU kinematic checks and recorded-input replay; native diagnostic pending
facts.text: The candidate matches swing and support motion around lift-off and touchdown. It permits inward foot motion during swing to retain joint bounds. It keeps yaw targets, motor limits and acceptance gates. Full-command, clearance, reset and early-touchdown checks pass within 177 locomotion tests. Native testing starts with the canonical 0.10 m/s case from two resets.

facts.title: We pass canonical forward walking from two resets
facts.backend: Isaac Sim; two 1000-control captures; approved 19-body robot
facts.text: Both independent resets pass the existing 0.10 m/s case. Mean planar error is 0.01931 m/s against 0.025; the computed torque-demand fraction is 0.00167 against 0.005. Native motor and contact checks pass. The first trial has 18.9–24.1 mm toe lift in low mode. Stops, raised clearance and terrain remain pending.
